title: Rotate Telegram bot token (lived in .env on attacker-touched VPS)
description: The Telegram bot token was in /opt/switch-berlin/app/.env on the box the attacker had partial access to during kb-vp8. Cheap to rotate. User-driven action: @BotFather → /revoke → reissue → update TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN in GH Actions secret + local .env + /etc/kb-backup/env on VPS. Source: 2026-05-13 consolidated security review, finding #7.
acceptance_criteria: Old token revoked at @BotFather. New token deployed via GH secret, propagated to .env on VPS, and to /etc/kb-backup/env. bot service + kb-backup alerts both functional with new token (run /healthcheck command, trigger kb-backup --test-alert).
close_reason: Token rotated 2026-05-14. /mybots → API Token → Show flow returned valid token; getMe pre-validation HTTP 200; propagated to GH secret, /etc/kb-backup/env, /opt/switch-berlin/app/.env via stdin-only flow (token never in agent transcript or argv argv-visible-to-agent). Bot container force-recreated (restart alone keeps old env); kb-backup --test-alert canary delivered to operator Telegram. Side-bead kb-j1l filed for /opt/switch-berlin/app/.env root:root ownership regression blocking redeploy; kb-wut filed for python-telegram-bot leaking token in InvalidToken log message.

title: Validate kb-backup dump size + alert on regression (size + OnFailure)
description: 2026-05-12 incident: backup script ran for ~12h overwriting good snapshots with empty ~3.5KiB dumps after the DB was wiped. The size-regression alert (kb-336) is already on prod. This bead tracks pulling that fix into the version-controlled copy in infra/ so a VPS rebuild doesn't lose it. Source: 2026-05-13 consolidated security review, finding #5.
acceptance_criteria: infra/kb-backup.sh aborts with non-zero exit if dump <50KiB AND alerts via Telegram. kb-backup.service has OnFailure= pointing at the alerting unit. Both behaviors land in repo, not just on VPS. Composes with kb-vms (pull script into infra/).

title: Add /healthz endpoint so external uptime probes can detect wipes <5min
description: accounts/middleware.py:14 already allowlists /healthz in ALWAYS_PUBLIC_PREFIXES but a_core/urls.py defines no route. The May-12 wipe was undetected for ~12h because nothing was looking. A 5-line view returning 200 when Event.objects.exists() else 503 would cut detection time to ~3min via free UptimeRobot. Source: 2026-05-13 consolidated security review, finding #4.
acceptance_criteria: GET /healthz returns 200 with a stable JSON body when Event table has rows, 503 when empty. URL routed in a_core/urls.py, view colocated with pages or a_core. Test covers both branches (empty + non-empty events). Operator follow-up: point UptimeRobot at https://switch.berlin/healthz with 5-min interval.

title: Remove insecure SECRET_KEY default from settings.py + rotate prod key
description: a_core/settings.py:13-16 falls back to a committed 'django-insecure-dev-only-replace-me-…' string if SECRET_KEY env is unset. If prod env is ever misconfigured → session forgery, password-reset token forgery, signed-URL forgery. Source: 2026-05-13 consolidated security review, finding #3.
acceptance_criteria: settings.py reads SECRET_KEY with no default (env.str('SECRET_KEY')) — Django crashes on boot if unset, not silently uses the public string. Local dev uses .env with a generated key. Operator follow-up: rotate SECRET_KEY GH secret + .env on prod since the default may have been latent at some point.

title: Pipe self-heal SQL via stdin so DB password doesn't land in remote argv
description: deploy.yml self-heal step (lines 124-130) runs psql -c "ALTER USER postgres WITH PASSWORD '${DB_PASS}'" — password visible in /proc/*/cmdline and remote shell history on every deploy. Source: 2026-05-13 consolidated security review, finding #2.
acceptance_criteria: deploy.yml self-heal pipes the ALTER USER statement via stdin (e.g., printf or heredoc into psql), not -c. $DB_PASS no longer appears in argv on the VPS. Self-heal still aligns role password with DATABASE_URL secret.

title: Fix docker-compose.yml POSTGRES_PASSWORD literal (wipe vector on fresh init)
description: docker-compose.yml:51 hardcodes POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres on the db service. The kb-vb7 self-heal step (deploy.yml:124-130) realigns the role to DATABASE_URL post-init, but any fresh volume init re-creates the role with password 'postgres' — back to the May-12 wipe vector. Source: 2026-05-13 consolidated security review, finding #1.
acceptance_criteria: docker-compose.yml db service reads POSTGRES_PASSWORD via ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD} interpolation (sourced from .env). Fresh volume init on prod gives role the rotated password, not 'postgres'. Self-heal step in deploy.yml remains as belt-and-suspenders.

title: Audit postgres + app secrets post-ransomware (rotate any potentially compromised)
description: kb-3w6 self-heal rotated the postgres superuser password; ensure no other secrets were compromised. Check: GH Actions secrets, .env on prod, any creds that may have been visible via pg_dump landing in DB_URL or logs. The prior postgres password was almost certainly known to the attacker (since they DROPed tables) — confirm rotation has propagated and the old password is invalid.
acceptance_criteria: All postgres-connecting clients (app, qcluster, bot, kb-backup) use rotated creds. GH secrets audited. Prior password proven invalid via psql -h switch.berlin -p ... from off-host (now closed, so this just means: pg_hba+password rotated).
close_reason: Post-incident credential rotation: DATABASE_URL + SECRET_KEY rotated on GH Secrets (host-agent driven, attempt 2 used correct stdin pattern after first attempt set both to literal '-'). deploy.yml hardened: POSTGRES_PASSWORD now derived from DATABASE_URL (literal 'postgres' removed from line 83); both render-.env and self-heal steps now scheme-prefix-check via 'case' + extract via 'sed -nE p' so a malformed secret fails loud instead of silently corrupting pg_authid. Live verification: HTTP 200 on /events/, all 4 containers healthy, Django check --database default clean. Commits: fba80fe (POSTGRES_PASSWORD derive), c17f088 (guards). Memory saved as gh-cli-gh-secret-set-name-body-does.

title: Production data loss: events/profiles/venues/users wiped 2026-05-11 evening
description: Operator-data tables empty on prod as of 2026-05-12. PGDATA initdb was 2026-05-11 08:45 UTC (single event) so wipe is via SQL ops, not volume swap. Window: 2026-05-11 16:59 CEST -> 2026-05-12 03:14 UTC (empty backup). django_migrations + auth_* survive; events_event, organizers_profile, venues_venue, accounts_(custom)user are 0 rows. Handoff in docs/handoff-2026-05-12-data-loss.md. Tasks: (1) finish root cause via pg_stat_database tup_deleted + docker logs + django_q schedules + management commands audit; (2) enumerate restic snapshots on BX11 to find latest pre-loss; (3) produce written restore plan for operator sign-off (DO NOT EXECUTE).
notes:
Root cause: PostgreSQL ransomware via 5432 (closed in 2af6a13). Ransom note in readme_to_recover db (BTC bc1qlmszwx8ehgmx38xdk9fwqrzxtw8cqvrnly4dt6, DATAID 39XE2, akilapsg campaign). Wipe window: 2026-05-11 16:59:47 UTC -> 2026-05-12 03:14:28 UTC. Latest pre-loss restic snapshot: ee28dab3 (db-20260511-165945.dump, ~133KiB). Restore plan: docs/incident-2026-05-12-data-loss-restore-plan.md — AWAITING OPERATOR APPROVAL.
Adversarial review (1 round) surfaced 15 findings. Blockers folded: F1+F15 (--clean is broken; switching to DROP DATABASE / CREATE DATABASE / pg_restore), F8 (RESTIC_PASSWORD via systemd-run+EnvironmentFile), F9 (bot last), F10 (stop kb-backup.timer), F2 (verify DB name), F6 (journalctl scrape). Lighter fold-ins: L1/L6, F11, F5. Exit: convergence. Rewriting plan in docs/incident-2026-05-12-data-loss-restore-plan.md.
close_reason: Restored from restic snapshot ee28dab3 (2026-05-11 16:59:45 UTC, 132.956 KiB pg_dump). Full execution log in docs/incident-2026-05-12-data-loss-restore-plan.md. Final state: 32 events, 3 profiles, 3 venues, 0 users (snapshot pre-dated Jonatan's signup), 90 migrations applied, /events/ and /p/iksk-berlin/ HTTP 200. Fresh post-restore snapshot f1357f35 (139.943 KiB) confirms data is back. Follow-ups: kb-vb7 (P0 secret audit), kb-336 (P1 backup-size alert), kb-u6p (P2 restore drill), kb-oam (P2 PG forensic logging).

title: docker-compose db: bind 5432 to 127.0.0.1 (close prod postgres to public internet)
description: docker-compose.yml maps db:5432:5432 to host without binding. On prod (switch.berlin) this exposes postgres to the public internet — db logs show active brute-force attempts including 'database "wog" does not exist' probes and 'GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE current_database() TO CURRENT_USER' injection attempts (see app-db-1 logs starting 2026-05-12 09:30 UTC). Change to 127.0.0.1:5432:5432 so the port is reachable only on the VPS itself (still works for in-host docker exec and SSH-tunnelled debugging). Discovered while root-causing kb-3w6.
acceptance_criteria: docker-compose.yml maps db port as '127.0.0.1:5432:5432' (not '5432:5432'). After deploy, ss/netstat on the VPS shows postgres listening only on 127.0.0.1, NOT on 0.0.0.0. nmap from off-host returns closed/filtered on 5432.
close_reason: Verified on prod 2026-05-13: docker-compose.yml binds 127.0.0.1:5432:5432 (commit 2af6a13), ss on VPS shows docker-proxy listening only on 127.0.0.1, no public exposure.

title: Stand up production deploy target for Switch Berlin
description:
Blocks kb-9hw (env-var rotation per ADR-006 D3). No production environment currently exists — everything runs against the local docker compose stack. Before kb-9hw can rotate the legal-contact env vars to public-facing values, the Switch Berlin app must be deployed somewhere reachable from the public internet on a real domain (switch.berlin), with all 4 legal pages (/impressum, /privacy, /terms, /takedown) live, q-cluster running, db migrations applied, manage.py check --deploy passing, and a verified nightly backup.

The gate model is **env-var rotation**, NOT flag-toggling — per ADR-006 D3 (FLEXIBLE) the system check fails if any IMPRESSUM_* is empty while PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED=True; internal-cohort posture is achieved by populating env vars with the maintainer's personal/operational values. kb-9hw rotates those values to switch.berlin-domain values once email/forwarding is configured.

Authoritative acceptance: see --design ## Acceptance contract (split A. External / B. On-host / C. Gate posture).
design:
## Context

Stand up a public production deploy target for the Switch Berlin app (codebase identifier `switch`; public domain `switch.berlin`). This bead blocks kb-9hw (the legal-gate completion per ADR-006 D3) — the gate is meaningless without a real environment to honour it *in*.

Constraints driving the decisions:
- **Single dev** (jsnyde0) deploying solo.
- **GDPR / EU data residency** — Berlin kink-community platform; user data must reside in EU jurisdiction.
- **Low traffic at v0** — single-VPS sizing is comfortable; no HA requirements yet.
- **Cost-sensitive** — personal project, target ≲ €15/mo total infra.
- **Existing dev stack** is `docker compose` (app + qcluster + bot + db services) — production should mirror dev to minimise dev/prod drift.

## Decisions

### D1: Hosting topology (FIRM)

**Decision:** Hetzner Cloud VPS (Falkenstein or Nuremberg region), Caddy as TLS-terminating reverse proxy, the existing docker compose stack running on the host.

**Rationale:**
- Cheapest path that satisfies EU data residency (~€4–8/mo for CX series).
- Compose-on-host mirrors the dev stack one-to-one — minimises dev/prod drift.
- Caddy handles TLS automatically (Let's Encrypt) with a one-line config; no manual cert management.
- Hetzner is EU-incorporated; reduces GDPR transfer-impact-assessment overhead vs US PaaS vendors.

**Alternatives:**

| Option | Rejected because | Warrant |
|---|---|---|
| Fly.io (Frankfurt region) | ~$15–30/mo realistic, US-incorporated (DPA still required), more vendor lock-in for marginal ergonomics gain at this scale. | cost + jurisdiction |
| Hetzner VPS + Coolify | Adds a self-hosted PaaS layer on top of the VPS — more moving parts to maintain for one dev, no payoff at v0. | complexity |
| Railway / Render | US-hosted by default; EU regions limited or extra cost. | jurisdiction |

**What would invalidate:** traffic grows past single-VPS comfort (~thousands req/min sustained), or we need multi-region HA, or operator decides to delegate ops to a managed PaaS.

### D2: Database hosting + backup posture (FIRM)

**Decision:** `pgvector/pgvector:pg17` container as the `db` compose service on the same VPS, bind-mounted data volume. Nightly `pg_dump` job pushes encrypted backups via `restic` to Hetzner Storage Box (~€3/mo for 1TB, EU). Backup schedule installed as a systemd timer `kb-backup.timer` (cron acceptable as a fallback if the host distro lacks systemd-timers in the default profile).

**Rationale:**
- Same image as dev → schema/extension parity, no surprises with pgvector.
- Off-host backup is the actual durability story; the on-host volume is convenience storage.
- Restic gives encrypted, deduplicated, versioned backups with point-in-time pruning policy.
- Systemd timers expose `Triggered at` / `LastTriggerUSec` introspection (`systemctl list-timers kb-backup.timer`) — observable schedule state is part of the acceptance contract.

**Alternatives:**

| Option | Rejected because | Warrant |
|---|---|---|
| Separate Hetzner VPS for DB + private network | ~doubles infra cost, no real benefit at v0 traffic. Restic backup already covers single-VPS-loss case. | cost |
| External managed Postgres (Neon EU / Supabase EU / Crunchy Bridge) | ~$20–30/mo, adds a second vendor + DPA, removes useful dev/prod parity. Reconsider when ops time becomes the bottleneck. | cost + simplicity |

**What would invalidate:** RTO/RPO requirements tighten below 24h, data volume outgrows Storage Box tier, or we need read replicas.

### D3: Domain, TLS, and host policy (FIRM)

**Decision:**
- **Domain (settled):** `switch.berlin` (already registered via inwx).
- **TLS provider:** Caddy with automatic Let's Encrypt for both `switch.berlin` (apex) and `www.switch.berlin` (redirected to apex via 301 or 308). Caddy `reverse_proxy` preserves the `Host:` header (default behaviour) so Django ALLOWED_HOSTS matching works unchanged.
- **Host policy:** Django `ALLOWED_HOSTS=switch.berlin,www.switch.berlin`; `CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=https://switch.berlin,https://www.switch.berlin`. Both rendered into `/opt/switch-berlin/.env` per D5's "non-secret env" subsection.

**Rationale:**
- Domain is already owned (sunk cost); renaming has zero upside.
- Caddy auto-renew removes a class of "expired cert at 3 AM" failure modes vs. Nginx + certbot, where cert rotation is a manually-installed cron job.
- Both apex and `www` served so typo-tolerance is preserved without forcing the user to memorise the bare apex.

**Alternatives:**

| Option | Rejected because | Warrant |
|---|---|---|
| Domain rename (any other) | Already registered + already rebranded everywhere downstream; no upside. | sunk cost |
| Nginx + certbot | Cert rotation lives in operator's crontab, not in the proxy config; one more failure mode to monitor. Adopt only if Caddy's TLS automation breaks for our use case. | operational simplicity |
| Cloudflare-fronted TLS (Cloudflare origin cert) | Adds a US-jurisdiction proxy in front of EU traffic, contradicts D1's data-residency rationale, and creates an opaque layer between us and TLS. | jurisdiction |
| Apex-only (no `www` CNAME) | Loses typo-tolerance; users who type `www.` get NXDOMAIN. Cost of adding `www` is one Caddy site block. | UX |

**What would invalidate:** brand changes, or we need a `*.switch.berlin` wildcard for tenant subdomains (which would mandate DNS-01 challenge instead of HTTP-01).

### D4: Deploy mechanism + secret-rendering ordering (FLEXIBLE on mechanism, FIRM on ordering)

**Decision:** GitHub Actions workflow triggered on push to `main`. The workflow's step ordering is **mandatory and ordered**:

1. SSH in as the deploy user, `git pull origin main` in `/opt/switch-berlin/app`.
2. **Render `.env` from GH Actions Secrets + non-secret workflow env (per D5) and `scp` to `/opt/switch-berlin/.env` (chmod 600, owned by deploy user)** — must complete before step 3. If the render or scp fails, abort the workflow.
3. `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file /opt/switch-berlin/.env build app` (the `docker-compose.prod.yml` overlay is created as part of this bead's scope; see D6).
4. `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file /opt/switch-berlin/.env up -d --remove-orphans`.
5. `docker compose exec app python manage.py migrate --no-input` (apply pending migrations).
6. `docker compose exec app python manage.py migrate --check` (post-condition verify — exit 0 ⇒ no migrations pending after the apply step).
7. `docker compose exec app python manage.py check --deploy` (fails the workflow if non-zero).
8. Force one immediate backup run via `systemctl start kb-backup.service` so the timer's `LAST` column populates before the acceptance contract is evaluated.

**Rationale:**
- Single dev → push-to-deploy is the right ergonomic level.
- No laptop dependency for hotfixes (push from anywhere).
- Builds run on the host, so nothing leaves the EU during deploy.
- Step 2 must precede steps 3–4 because Compose `env_file:` resolves on container-start; a stale or missing `.env` produces a silently-misconfigured boot. Compose's `env_file:` directive treats a missing file as a hard error, which is the desired fail-closed behaviour.
- Step 5 (apply) precedes step 6 (verify) because `migrate --check` exits non-zero when migrations ARE pending — running it before `migrate` would fail the workflow on every deploy that has a pending migration.

**Alternatives:**

| Option | Rejected because | Warrant |
|---|---|---|
| Manual SSH + `deploy.sh` | Forces operator-on-laptop for every deploy; loses the "push from phone in emergency" property. | ergonomics |
| Build image in CI, push to GHCR, pull on host | Cleanest separation, fastest deploys, but more YAML to maintain at v0. Promote to this when host-side rebuild times become annoying. | complexity |

**What would invalidate:** rebuild-on-host takes long enough to interrupt a deploy window, or we need image provenance / signing.

### D5: Secrets + non-secret env management (FIRM)

**Decision:** GitHub Actions Secrets is the source-of-truth for secret values. The deploy workflow renders an `.env` file from those secrets *plus* a small set of non-secret env vars defined in the workflow YAML, and `scp`s the result to `/opt/switch-berlin/.env` on the VPS (chmod 600, owned by deploy user). Docker compose `env_file:` reads it. Ordering is enforced per D4.

**Secrets in scope (set in GH Actions Secrets):**

*Django + framework:*
- `SECRET_KEY` (read by `a_core/settings.py:13` as `env.str("SECRET_KEY", ...)`)
- `DATABASE_URL`

*ADR-006 D3 legal-page env vars:*
- `IMPRESSUM_NAME`
- `IMPRESSUM_ADDRESS`
- `IMPRESSUM_EMAIL`
- `IMPRESSUM_PHONE` (optional per §5 TMG, rendered if set)
- `RESPONSIBLE_PERSON_NAME` (§18 MStV; defaults to `IMPRESSUM_NAME` in settings)
- `RESPONSIBLE_PERSON_ADDRESS` (§18 MStV; defaults to `IMPRESSUM_ADDRESS`)
- `DSA_CONTACT_EMAIL` (DSA Art. 11; defaults to `IMPRESSUM_EMAIL`)

*Integrations:*
- `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`
- `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY`

*Future-reserved (set when feature lands):* `LOGFIRE_TOKEN`, etc.

**Non-secret env vars also rendered into `/opt/switch-berlin/.env` (defined in workflow YAML, not GH Secrets):**
- `ALLOWED_HOSTS=switch.berlin,www.switch.berlin`
- `CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=https://switch.berlin,https://www.switch.berlin`
- `DEBUG=False`
- `DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=a_core.settings`

**Rationale:**
- GH Actions Secrets gives a centralized, audit-logged management UI.
- Operator laptop never has to hold secrets — losing the laptop is fine.
- Re-running the deploy workflow can rebuild a fresh VPS from scratch (disaster recovery is part of the daily-driver path).
- Smaller blast radius than `sops`-in-repo: secrets are not in git history at all.
- Splitting secret vs. non-secret in the render step keeps configuration values (host policy, debug flag) out of the GH Secrets vault where they don't belong, while still landing in the same `.env` file the container reads.

**Alternatives:**

| Option | Rejected because | Warrant |
|---|---|---|
| Host-resident `.env` only, CI never sees secrets | "Lose laptop + lose VPS = lose secrets" risk; most of these secrets *are* regeneratable but rotation friction is higher. Centralized rotation in GH UI is materially better for one dev. | recoverability |
| sops-encrypted `.env.enc` in repo + age key on VPS | Most overhead for a one-dev project; no compelling audit benefit yet. Promote if/when team grows. | complexity |

**What would invalidate:** team grows to ≥2 people and we need per-environment secret scoping, or a regulator requires a specific secret-storage attestation, or GH org compromise threat model changes.

### D6: Compose service layout + prod overlay (FIRM)

**Decision:** All processes run as separate compose services on the same VPS, mirroring the dev stack 1:1:

| Service | Image / process | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `app` | repo-built; runs Gunicorn | Django HTTP |
| `qcluster` | repo-built; runs `manage.py qcluster` | django-q2 worker |
| `bot` | repo-built; runs the Telegram bot entrypoint | Telegram bot long-poll |
| `db` | `pgvector/pgvector:pg17` (per D2) | Postgres + pgvector |

**Files in scope of this bead:**
- The repo's existing `docker-compose.yml` is the base layer (used in dev).
- A new `docker-compose.prod.yml` overlay is created as part of this bead's scope. It adds: `restart: unless-stopped` on every service, host-mounted bind volume paths under `/opt/switch-berlin/`, and any prod-only resource limits. It does NOT add or override services.

**Rationale:**
- Mirrors the dev stack 1:1 — no new failure modes introduced at deploy.
- One-process-per-container makes logs / metrics / OOM diagnosis straightforward.
- Restart policy lives in the prod overlay, not the base file, so dev compose runs without auto-restart spam during iteration.

**Alternatives:**

| Option | Rejected because | Warrant |
|---|---|---|
| All-in-one container with supervisord | Process supervision becomes our problem rather than Docker's; harder to debug. | operability |
| Workers on a second VPS | Premature isolation; doubles infra cost without solving any current problem. | cost |
| `restart: unless-stopped` in base compose file | Causes unwanted auto-restart cycles during dev iteration (e.g., when intentionally killing a service to test failure modes). | dev ergonomics |

**What would invalidate:** workers consume enough CPU to starve the web tier, or we need geographic separation for queue durability.

### D7: Static files (FLEXIBLE)

**Decision:** Whitenoise serves Django static files; `collectstatic` runs at image build time. Caddy passes through (no separate file_server route).

**Rationale:**
- Standard Django pattern; near-zero config.
- Caddy provides compression + caching headers in front.
- Sufficient up to thousands of req/sec.

**Alternatives:**

| Option | Rejected because | Warrant |
|---|---|---|
| Caddy `file_server` from a named volume | Marginal latency improvement; more compose wiring; not measurably better at v0. | premature optimization |
| S3 / Hetzner Object Storage + django-storages | Useful when user-uploaded media exists; deferred until that lands. | scope |

**What would invalidate:** user-uploaded media (avatars, event photos) ships, at which point object storage becomes the right home for media (and possibly static).

### D8: Artifact shape — epic-only with follow-up extraction (FIRM, per /brainstorm-v2 skill discipline + ADR-006 D11 once authored)

**Decision:** kb-6nq is **epic-only**. The decisions narrative lives on `--design` (this document). No paired ADR is written by design-v2.

**However:** a separate follow-up bead (kb-dle, already filed) extracts the *durable* principles into an ADR *after* the deploy is live. Three candidate principles to evaluate post-deploy for promotion to FIRM ADR-status:
1. **EU data residency requirement** — applies to any future infra choice, not just this Hetzner box. *(Strongest re-derivability case: GDPR Art. 44 transfer rules are an external constraint; a fresh agent without an ADR could re-derive "US PaaS is fine" incorrectly.)*
2. **Secrets-managed-in-CI, not on operator laptops** — security posture that should outlive any specific hosting choice. *(External constraint: rotation/recoverability/audit posture; without an ADR a fresh agent could re-derive "host-only `.env` is fine" incorrectly.)*
3. **Dev/prod stack parity via compose** — load-bearing rationale across D1, D2, D6. *Not yet asserted as durable*: the parity rationale is currently anchored only in cross-decision cohesion within kb-6nq itself, not in an external constraint. kb-dle's job at evaluation time is to determine whether parity actually paid off operationally (e.g., did a dev-side change actually catch a prod-bound bug?), or whether the cohesion was illusory and the principle should be discarded.

**Rationale (re-derivability test):**
- Imagine all implementation deleted, fresh agent given only the ADR set: would they need to know we picked **Hetzner specifically** (vs Fly / Railway / a different VPS provider)? **No** — they'd re-derive from constraints (single dev, EU/GDPR, ~€15/mo budget, low traffic).
- Same answer for Caddy-vs-Nginx, GH-Actions-vs-Ansible, whitenoise-vs-CDN — these are tactical choices that should *not* clutter the ADR set.
- The first two extracted principles, by contrast, *would* be re-derived incorrectly without an ADR. The third (dev/prod parity) is the open question kb-dle is filed to resolve with operational evidence.
- Writing the ADR *after* operational experience means it's grounded in what actually broke / worked, not speculation.

**Alternatives:**

| Option | Rejected because | Warrant |
|---|---|---|
| ADR-paired now | Decisions are claimed-not-tested; locking them as FIRM ADR before first contact with prod risks codifying the wrong things. | epistemic — review-after-evidence is cheaper |
| Epic-only with no follow-up | Risks burying the durable principles inside a tactical bead; future agents wouldn't find them when re-deriving infra choices. | discoverability |

**What would invalidate:** if the deploy uncovers a fourth principle worth ADR-status, kb-dle's scope grows to capture it.

*Citation note:* the artifact-shape decision rule (epic-only vs ADR-paired as a first-class decision per the re-derivability test) is enforced by the /brainstorm-v2 skill description. The skill text references "ADR-006 D11" but ADR-006 currently contains only D1-D3; D11 is a planned-but-unwritten section. Treat the skill as the authoritative source until D11 is materialised.

## Acceptance contract

The acceptance contract is split by **probe mode** so a future verifier can reproduce pass/fail unambiguously.

### A. External probes (run from any internet-connected client; no VPS access required)

**Given** the GitHub Actions deploy workflow has run to completion on a push to `main`,

**When** an anonymous browser (no auth, no session) requests each of the four legal pages:
- `https://switch.berlin/impressum`
- `https://switch.berlin/privacy`
- `https://switch.berlin/terms`
- `https://switch.berlin/takedown`

**Then** each URL returns HTTP 200 with a response body containing the page's expected `<h1>` heading (`Impressum`, `Privacy`, `Terms`, `Takedown` — case-insensitive match acceptable),

**And** at least one referenced static asset on each of the four pages (i.e., a `<link rel="stylesheet">` or `<script src=...>` URL parsed from the page's HTML) returns HTTP 200 with a `Content-Type` matching the asset extension (`text/css`, `application/javascript`, `image/svg+xml`, etc.),

**And** TLS termination uses a Let's Encrypt-issued certificate, verified by:
```
openssl s_client -connect switch.berlin:443 -servername switch.berlin </dev/null 2>/dev/null \
  | openssl x509 -noout -issuer
```
producing an issuer line whose `O =` field is `Let's Encrypt` (i.e., the issuer Organization, not just CN — robust to LE intermediate CN rotations like R10/R11/E5/E6). Self-signed certs and any other CA Organization are failures.

**And** `https://www.switch.berlin/...` redirects to `https://switch.berlin/...` (HTTP 301 or 308).

### B. On-host probes (run by deploy user via SSH on the VPS)

**And** `docker compose exec app python manage.py migrate --check` exits 0 (no unapplied migrations),

**And** `docker compose exec app python manage.py check --deploy` exits 0 against production settings,

**And** `docker compose ps --format json` shows `app`, `qcluster`, `bot`, `db` services all in `running` state with `Health: healthy` (or no healthcheck defined, with status `running`),

**And** `systemctl list-timers kb-backup.timer` (or equivalent cron entry) shows the timer is enabled, scheduled, and has triggered at least once (`LAST` column populated, not `n/a`) — D4 step 8 forces an immediate backup run during deploy to populate this on first deploy,

**And** the latest restic snapshot in Hetzner Storage Box (verified via `restic snapshots --last 1`) restores successfully into a scratch container on the VPS, and:
  - if the live database's `events_event` table is non-empty: the restored row count matches the live row count within ±1 (allowing for in-flight writes),
  - if `events_event` is empty: `pg_dump --schema-only` of the restored DB produces a checksum identical to `pg_dump --schema-only` of the live DB (verifying the restic round-trip transferred actual data, not the empty-DB trivial pass).

### C. Gate posture (env-var rotation model, per ADR-006 D3)

**And** the deploy environment is in **internal-cohort posture**, defined by:
- `IMPRESSUM_EMAIL` is set to the maintainer's current personal/operational address (`kinkybubbles@protonmail.com`), NOT a `@switch.berlin` address.
- `PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED=True` (flag is True as seeded by `a_core/migrations/0003_seed_featureflags.py:9`); the gate that prevents premature public posture is **env-var-population**, not flag-toggling.
- `manage.py check --deploy` therefore exits 0 (all `IMPRESSUM_*` populated, even with personal values) — satisfying acceptance B.

**Note on consequence:** under this posture, `switch.berlin` IS publicly reachable post-deploy. The Impressum will display the maintainer's `@protonmail.com` address. This is the explicit ADR-006 D3 (FLEXIBLE) design — internal-cohort use with placeholder values populated by the maintainer's personal email is the supported state until the operator rotates env vars.

**kb-9hw's actual job (per this gate model):** rotate `IMPRESSUM_EMAIL` (and any other contact env vars) to public-facing values once email/forwarding is configured at the switch.berlin domain via inwx, then promote the URL through whatever announcement channels apply. kb-9hw is an **env-var rotation + announcement** moment, not a flag-toggle.

This was the original ADR-006 D3 model; the previous "flag stays False" framing of acceptance C was a misreading that round-2 review surfaced (finding F6).

Also eliminates a remote-side world-readable secret-exposure window (no staging file on /tmp). Pattern mirrors the existing Caddyfile sudo-install step. title: [schema-3/5] Add EventFacilitator M2M (Lavinia teaches at IKSK events)
description: Third child of kb-3bs. Depends on kb-3bs-1 (Profile model exists). Add EventFacilitator through-table (event, profile, role, order). role is free-text (Lead, Co-facilitator, DJ, Doula, Host, etc.). Add Event.facilitators = M2M(Profile, through=EventFacilitator). Wire into event_detail and event_drawer templates: render "Facilitated by Lavinia (Lead), Mira (Host)". On Profile page, list 'Events facilitated' alongside 'Events organized'. (Optional, separate ticket if scope grows: seed Xplore Berlin with its facilitator list). ADRs: ADR-007 D2, D4.
design:
## Context

Per ADR-007 D2 (FIRM) the schema needs a separate `EventFacilitator` through-table distinct from `EventOrganizer` (just shipped in kb-n0y, commit 7f18a71). The reason for the split (not consolidation): querying 'events organized by X' vs 'events facilitated by X' is a frequent UX need (profile page tabs, search filters), and the legal/financial responsibility (organizer) vs leads-the-activity (facilitator) distinction is semantically real. Lavinia teaches a 'Silent Hunger' workshop organized by IKSK — she should appear as a facilitator on that event, not an organizer.

V0 today has no facilitator concept; named human facilitators live in description strings only. After this bead, an event can declare zero-or-more facilitators with a free-text role.

## Design (per ADR-007 D2, FIRM split)

Add `EventFacilitator(event, profile, role, order)` through-model and `Event.facilitators = M2M(Profile, through=EventFacilitator)`. Purely additive — no existing fields move or get dropped.

**Field shape:**
- `event` FK(Event, on_delete=CASCADE, related_name='event_facilitator_set')
- `profile` FK(organizers.Profile, on_delete=PROTECT, related_name='facilitated_event_set')
- `role` CharField(max_length=100, blank=True) — free text: 'Lead', 'Co-facilitator', 'DJ', 'Doula', 'Host', ''. blank=True so an unrole'd facilitator is allowed (just 'a facilitator').
- `order` IntegerField(default=0) — for stable display ordering.
- `created_at` DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)

**M2M shape:**
- `Event.facilitators = M2M(Profile, through=EventFacilitator, related_name='events_facilitated', blank=True)`
- Reverse: `profile.events_facilitated.all()` returns events this profile facilitates.

**No partial-unique constraint:** unlike EventOrganizer's is_primary, a Profile can appear once per Event as a facilitator with any role. We do enforce `unique_together = ('event', 'profile')` so the same person doesn't get listed twice as a facilitator on the same event (different roles can still be expressed by changing role text on the single row).

**Same profile in both tables:** per ADR-007 D2, the same Profile may be both organizer and facilitator of the same Event (Lavinia organizes her own workshop AND leads it). No cross-table constraint blocks this — the two through-tables are independent.

**Admin:** add `EventFacilitatorInline` in `events/admin.py` alongside the existing `EventOrganizerInline` (added by kb-n0y). No public form for adding facilitators yet — admin-only.

**Migration:** single migration, additive only. CreateModel EventFacilitator + AddField facilitators M2M. No data migration needed (V0 has no existing facilitator data).

**Templates/views:** out of scope for this bead. `event.facilitators.all()` becomes available but no template renders it yet. A follow-up UI bead can surface facilitators on event detail / drawer when desired — that's a separate concern from the schema change.

## Risk

Low. Purely additive. No existing call site references `Event.facilitators` (grep confirms) so nothing can break. The new admin inline mirrors the EventOrganizer pattern from kb-n0y.

The only nuance: `Event.event_facilitator_set` reverse name collides with nothing (Django auto-creates this for the through-FK; verified no existing model uses it).

## Scope boundary (what this bead does NOT do)

- No public form for adding facilitators (admin-only).
- No template renders facilitators (separate UI bead).
- No 'feature events facilitated by X' page on Profile (separate UI bead).
- No data migration from description strings (manual admin curation handles existing events as needed).

## ADRs consulted

ADR-007 D2 (FIRM split into separate organizer + facilitator through-tables), ADR-007 D4 (FLEXIBLE: 'Host' role maps to EventFacilitator.role='Host'), ADR-001 D8 (normalized from day 1).
acceptance_criteria:
After this bead ships, all of the following are observable:

1. **Model exists:** `events.models.EventFacilitator` is a Django model importable from `events.models`. It has fields: `event` FK(Event, on_delete=CASCADE), `profile` FK(organizers.Profile, on_delete=PROTECT), `role` CharField(max_length=100, blank=True), `order` IntegerField(default=0), `created_at` DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True).

2. **M2M field:** `Event._meta.get_field('facilitators')` returns a ManyToManyField. `Event.facilitators` resolves to a M2M manager via through=EventFacilitator. Adding a Profile via `event.event_facilitator_set.create(profile=p, role='Lead')` makes `p in event.facilitators.all()` True.

3. **Reverse accessor:** `profile.events_facilitated.all()` returns a queryset of Events where this Profile is a facilitator.

4. **Unique-together:** attempting to create two EventFacilitator rows with the same (event, profile) raises IntegrityError. Different role values do NOT bypass this (the (event, profile) tuple is the uniqueness key, not the (event, profile, role) tuple).

5. **Same profile both organizer + facilitator:** a Profile that is already an organizer of an Event (via EventOrganizer) can also be added as a facilitator of the same Event (via EventFacilitator) without IntegrityError. The two through-tables are independent.

6. **Blank role allowed:** creating an EventFacilitator with `role=''` succeeds (no validation error).

7. **Admin inline:** the Django admin for Event includes an `EventFacilitatorInline` (TabularInline or StackedInline), so curators can add facilitators in the Event admin page without needing a separate model admin URL.

8. **Migration clean:** `DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/postgres uv run python manage.py migrate` runs cleanly forward from main (commit 7f18a71). `uv run python manage.py makemigrations --dry-run` reports 'No changes detected' after the migration is applied.

9. **Full suite green:** `DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/postgres uv run pytest` passes all tests (≥996 passed, baseline from kb-n0y). No pre-existing test regresses.

10. **Lint clean:** `uv run ruff check .` introduces zero new errors compared to baseline.

11. **TDD evidence:** at least one test file in `events/tests/` (e.g. `test_event_facilitator_m2m.py`) exercises clauses 1-6 above with explicit assertions: model fields, M2M shape, reverse accessor, unique-together, dual-role profile, blank-role facilitator.
notes:
ADRs: ADR-007 D2, D4, ADR-001 D8.

Purely additive schema change. No data migration (V0 has no facilitator data). No existing call sites reference Event.facilitators, so backwards compat is trivially preserved.

Same-profile-both-roles: explicitly allowed per ADR-007 D2 — Lavinia organizes AND leads her own workshop. The two through-tables are independent.

UI rendering deferred to a separate follow-up bead. This schema-only bead unblocks admin curation; templates surfacing facilitators come later.
close_reason: EventFacilitator M2M shipped (ADR-007 D2). Additive: through-table + Event.facilitators M2M + admin inline. Same profile can be organizer+facilitator. Full suite green (≥1016).

## Context

First child of kb-3bs (Profile-centric schema migration per ADR-007). Today's V0 schema in `organizers/models.py` has `Organizer` with name/slug/description/avatar/website/telegram_channel + curation fields (status, verified_badge, approved_at/by, consent_recorded_at/method/notes, hidden) + community fields (follower_count, avg_rating, rating_count). `Event.organizer` is a single FK; `OrganizerFollow(user, organizer)` is the only follow mechanism. The model cannot represent named human facilitators (Lavinia) as first-class actors — they live in description strings.

## Design (per ADR-007 D1 + D5, FIRM)

Rename `Organizer` → `Profile` with a `kind` discriminator and a claimable User link. Single table, single slug namespace, single follow/claim/badge/moderation system serving both humans and collectives. The downstream beads (kb-n0y/qhl/ldo/ltr) all depend on Profile existing.

**D1 superset field set** (per ADR-007):
- `kind` enum: `person` | `collective` (no default in code; admin/ingestion must set explicitly per ADR-007 Risk note)
- Existing fields preserved verbatim: `name`, `slug`, `description`, `avatar`, `website`, `status`, `verified_badge`, `approved_at`, `approved_by`, `consent_recorded_at`, `consent_method`, `consent_notes`, `hidden`, `follower_count`, `avg_rating`, `rating_count`
- Renamed: `telegram_channel` → `telegram_link`
- New: `pronouns` (CharField, blank=True — mostly for kind=person but optional for either)
- New (D5 claim mechanism): `claimed_by` FK(User, null=True, on_delete=SET_NULL), `claimed_at` (DateTimeField, null=True)

**Scope boundary (what this bead does NOT do):**
- Does NOT convert `Event.organizer` FK to M2M (that's kb-n0y; deferred to keep this slot's risk profile low)
- Does NOT add `EventFacilitator` (kb-qhl)
- Does NOT unify `OrganizerFollow` (kb-ldo)
- Does NOT add `/p/{slug}/` route (kb-ltr); `/organizers/{slug}/` continues working unchanged this iteration

**Implementation choice (deferred — see Open):** keep the Django app dir name `organizers/` and rename only internals (the model class `Organizer` → `Profile`, admin, querysets, references) vs full app rename to `profiles/`. The decomposition pass should answer this.

## Risk

Production DB has curated rows. Migration must preserve data (Django `RenameModel` operation is the safe path) and all FKs (`Event.organizer`, `OrganizerFollow.organizer`) must redirect to the renamed model without losing rows.

## ADRs consulted

ADR-007 (D1 FIRM unified Profile model; D5 FIRM claimable via User FK), ADR-001 D8 (normalized from day 1), ADR-001 D1 (curated trust model — `status=candidate|approved|suspended` must keep working), ADR-006 D2 (legitimate-interest LIA continues to apply per Profile of kind=collective).
acceptance_criteria:
After this bead ships, all of the following are observable:

1. `organizers.models.Profile` is the model class name in the codebase; `Organizer` no longer exists as a class. The DB table backing it still holds every row that was in `organizers_organizer` before migration (row count preserved).
2. `Profile._meta.get_field('kind').choices` contains `person` and `collective`. `Profile._meta.get_field('pronouns')` exists. `Profile._meta.get_field('claimed_by')` is a nullable FK to `auth.User`. `Profile._meta.get_field('claimed_at')` is a nullable DateTimeField. `Profile._meta.get_field('telegram_link')` exists; `telegram_channel` does NOT exist on Profile.
3. Every pre-existing `Organizer` row is present as a `Profile` row with `kind='collective'`, the same slug, and the same id.
4. `Event.organizer` FK still resolves: an existing Event whose organizer-FK pointed to organizer id N now points to Profile id N (no orphan rows).
5. `OrganizerFollow.organizer` FK still resolves to the renamed model (kb-ldo will replace this table; this bead only keeps it functional).
6. `python manage.py migrate` runs cleanly forward from main; `python manage.py makemigrations --dry-run` reports "No changes detected" after the migration is applied.
7. The full project test suite passes on the renamed model. Tests that previously instantiated `Organizer(...)` now instantiate `Profile(...)` (or use a factory that returns Profile) and still pass.
8. `ruff check .` is clean. No stale imports of `from organizers.models import Organizer` remain (grep returns zero hits).
9. The URL `/organizers/{slug}/` continues to render the organizer/profile page (kb-ltr handles the redirect to `/p/`; this bead must NOT 404 it).
notes: ADRs: ADR-007, ADR-001 D8. Acceptance: bd lint warns no missing acceptance section.

title: [schema-2/5] Convert Event.organizer FK → EventOrganizer M2M (co-organizers)
description: Second child of kb-3bs. Depends on kb-3bs-1 (Profile model exists). Add EventOrganizer through-table (event, profile, is_primary, order) with partial unique constraint (one is_primary per event). Add Event.organizers = M2M(Profile, through=EventOrganizer). Data migration: each existing Event.organizer FK → EventOrganizer(profile=organizer_profile, is_primary=True, order=0). Add Event.primary_organizer property/manager method. Update all read sites: event_list (markers_geojson generation uses org_slug), event_drawer, event_detail templates, admin, search filters, tests. Drop Event.organizer FK after the M2M is fully wired and verified. ADRs: ADR-007 D2.
design:
## Context

Today's V0 schema has `Event.organizer` as a single FK to `organizers.Profile` (events/models.py:40-46), with two DB constraints keyed on it: `event_slug_unique_per_organizer` (organizer+slug) and `event_dup_guard_org_start_title` (organizer+start+title). Two indexes also include `organizer`. `Profile.events` reverse manager exists via `related_name='events'`. The attribute `event.organizer` is referenced across ~30 files: events/admin.py, events/views.py, organizers/views.py, ingestion/tasks_flags.py, templates (event_drawer, detail, _event_list, organizer_mini_card, attend button), tests, fixtures, seed commands.

Per ADR-007 D2 (FIRM split), each Event has one Profile as primary organizer plus zero-or-more co-organizers, represented via an `EventOrganizer` through-table with `is_primary: bool` (at most one True per event) and `order: int`. The single FK cannot express "IKSK × KACHENKA".

## Design (per ADR-007 D2, FIRM)

Add `EventOrganizer(event, profile, is_primary, order)` through-model and `Event.organizers = M2M(Profile, through=EventOrganizer)`. Drop `Event.organizer` FK after data is migrated.

**Compat surface (load-bearing):** preserve `event.organizer` as a Python @property returning the primary Profile (or None). This means ~30 references across templates/views/admin/ingestion/tests do NOT need touching; they keep working through the property. New code uses `event.organizers.all()` (queryset) or `event.primary_organizer` (alias to .organizer property).

**Profile reverse accessors:** `Profile.events` (the old FK reverse) is replaced by `Profile.events_organized` (M2M reverse from `Event.organizers`). To preserve the existing `profile.events.all()` call site in organizers/views.py:107 (`organizer.reviews.get(author=request.user)` actually uses reviews, not events — but other call sites do exist), expose `Profile.events` as a Python @property returning `self.events_organized` for compat.

**Constraints migration:** the two unique constraints on Event (slug-per-organizer, dup-guard org+start+title) lose their FK column. Replace them with constraints scoped via the primary EventOrganizer:
- `event_slug_unique_per_organizer` → drop entirely; add a UniqueConstraint on `EventOrganizer(profile, event__slug)` is impossible cross-model. Pragmatic V0: drop the slug-per-organizer constraint; rely on application-level slug uniqueness in admin/ingestion. Document this in --notes.
- `event_dup_guard_org_start_title` → drop entirely; replace with a model-level `Event.clean()` check or DB-level constraint on (start, title) alone. For V0, drop the constraint (the dup-guard was already weak — same org running two distinct workshops at the same start is legitimate).

**Indexes:** `Index(fields=['organizer', 'start'])` → drop; replace with `Index` on `EventOrganizer(profile, event)` (or rely on M2M's automatic index).

**Migration strategy (data-preserving, single migration file):**
1. CreateModel EventOrganizer with FK(event), FK(profile), is_primary, order, created_at.
2. AddField Event.organizers M2M(Profile, through=EventOrganizer).
3. Add partial unique constraint: "at most one EventOrganizer with is_primary=True per event" (PostgreSQL partial unique index via `UniqueConstraint(condition=Q(is_primary=True), fields=['event'])`).
4. RunPython data migration: for every Event with organizer_id IS NOT NULL, create EventOrganizer(event=event, profile=event.organizer, is_primary=True, order=0). Skip Events where organizer_id IS NULL.
5. RemoveConstraint event_slug_unique_per_organizer, event_dup_guard_org_start_title.
6. RemoveIndex events__organizer__start_idx.
7. RemoveField Event.organizer.

**Scope boundary (what this bead does NOT do):**
- Does NOT add EventFacilitator (kb-qhl).
- Does NOT change `Event.organizer` references throughout the codebase to use the new M2M API — the @property compat surface handles backwards compatibility. New features should prefer `event.organizers.all()`.
- Does NOT touch templates (the @property covers them).
- Does NOT add UI for adding co-organizers (admin still curates via the through-table inline; no public form).

## Risk

- ~30 files reference `event.organizer` — if the @property compat surface is wrong (e.g. returns the queryset instead of a single Profile), every template breaks. The contract demands `event.organizer` returns a Profile-or-None, identical to the FK semantics.
- The data migration must not lose any Event→Profile association. Verify row counts before/after: `Event.objects.filter(organizer__isnull=False).count() == EventOrganizer.objects.filter(is_primary=True).count()`.
- Dropping the unique constraints is a real product decision (recorded in --notes). If we later need slug-per-organizer uniqueness, it must be enforced at app level.

## ADRs consulted

ADR-007 D2 (FIRM: two through-tables, EventOrganizer with is_primary), ADR-007 D4 (FLEXIBLE: 'hosting organizer' = is_primary=True), ADR-001 D8 (normalized from day 1).
acceptance_criteria:
After this bead ships, all of the following are observable:

1. **Model:** `events.models.EventOrganizer` exists as a Django model with fields: `event` FK(Event, on_delete=CASCADE), `profile` FK(organizers.Profile, on_delete=PROTECT), `is_primary` BooleanField, `order` IntegerField (default=0), `created_at` DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True).

2. **M2M:** `Event.organizers` is a ManyToManyField to Profile, through=EventOrganizer. `Event._meta.get_field('organizers')` returns a ManyToManyField. The reverse accessor `Profile.events_organized` returns a queryset of Events.

3. **FK gone:** `Event._meta.get_field('organizer')` raises FieldDoesNotExist. The DB column `events_event.organizer_id` no longer exists.

4. **Compat property:** `event.organizer` is a Python @property returning the primary Profile-or-None (NOT a queryset). For an Event with one EventOrganizer(is_primary=True, profile=P), `event.organizer == P`. For an Event with no organizers, `event.organizer is None`. `event.primary_organizer` is an alias returning the same value.

5. **Profile.events compat:** `profile.events` returns a Django Manager/QuerySet of Events that resolves to all Events where this Profile is an organizer (any is_primary value). `profile.events.all()` works at every existing call site without raising AttributeError.

6. **Partial unique constraint:** attempting to save two EventOrganizer rows with the same event and `is_primary=True` raises IntegrityError. Saving multiple EventOrganizer rows for the same event with `is_primary=False` succeeds.

7. **Data migration:** for every pre-existing Event with `organizer_id IS NOT NULL` before migration, there is exactly one EventOrganizer row after migration with `event=that_event, is_primary=True, profile=the_original_organizer`. Row count assertion: `EventOrganizer.objects.filter(is_primary=True).count() == <pre-migration Event-with-organizer count>`.

8. **Constraints removed:** `event_slug_unique_per_organizer` and `event_dup_guard_org_start_title` are removed from Event._meta.constraints (or no longer apply because the field they reference is gone). The migration does not fail on existing duplicate rows.

9. **Migrations clean:** `uv run python manage.py migrate` runs cleanly forward from main. `uv run python manage.py makemigrations --dry-run` reports 'No changes detected' after the migration is applied.

10. **Full suite green:** `uv run pytest` passes all tests. Specifically, pre-existing tests that use `event.organizer` (events/tests/test_views.py, events/admin.py admin display, templates/events/_event_drawer.html via test_views_markers, ingestion/tests/test_pipeline.py) continue to pass without modification — the @property compat surface covers them.

11. **Lint clean:** `uv run ruff check .` is clean.

12. **TDD evidence:** at least one test exists in events/tests/ (or organizers/tests/) that exercises (a) creating an Event with multiple organizers via EventOrganizer through-rows, (b) the partial-unique constraint on is_primary, (c) the `event.organizer` compat property returning the primary Profile, (d) the data migration's preservation of the FK→primary mapping (a migration test or fixture-based assertion).
notes:
ADRs: ADR-007 D2, D4, ADR-001 D8.

Compat-surface decision: Event.organizer becomes a Python @property over EventOrganizer rows where is_primary=True. Rationale: ~30 files reference event.organizer (templates/views/admin/ingestion/tests). The property keeps all those call sites working unchanged. New code prefers event.organizers.all() (queryset) or event.primary_organizer (explicit).

Constraint removal: event_slug_unique_per_organizer and event_dup_guard_org_start_title are dropped because their FK column goes away. Slug-per-organizer uniqueness is no longer DB-enforced. Admin/ingestion should validate at app level if needed. Dup-guard was already weak — same org can legitimately run two distinct workshops at the same start. If pressure resurfaces, file a follow-up bead.
close_reason: Event.organizer FK → EventOrganizer M2M (ADR-007 D2). Compat @property preserves event.organizer / event.primary_organizer / profile.events.all(). Data migration preserves all FK→primary mappings. Full suite green (996 passed).

title: Cluster click silently no-ops on prod — maplibre 5.x dropped callback API (kb-k7a regression)
description:
Verified live on switch.berlin/events/: clicking the IKSK cluster does NOT open the popup AND does NOT zoom. Both branches of the kb-k7a fix are dead.

Root cause: maplibre-gl 5.2.0 (loaded from unpkg in _base.html) dropped the callback variant of GeoJSONSource.getClusterLeaves() and getClusterExpansionZoom(). Both methods now return a Promise. The callback passed as the 4th/2nd argument is silently ignored. No error is thrown.

Proof: a script that calls src.getClusterLeaves(cid, pc, 0, cb) with cb never fires. The same call awaited as a Promise returns the 17 leaves immediately.

Live cluster state today (zoom 10.56, default fit-bounds): 17 events cluster (16 IKSK at 13.426321,52.511692 + 1 KACHENKA at 13.402,52.519). With 2 unique coords, the intended branch is zoom-to-expand — which is also broken because getClusterExpansionZoom uses the same dead API.
acceptance_criteria: Cluster click on switch.berlin/events/ either opens the events-list popup (if all leaves share a coord) or zooms in to expand the cluster (if mixed). Verified live in browser-automation after deploy.
notes:
Fix is small: await src.getClusterLeaves(clusterId, pointCount, 0) and await src.getClusterExpansionZoom(clusterId) in static/js/events/map.js lines 194 and 237.

kb-k7a's close reviewer signoff did not run live verification — adds to the pattern documented in the alpine-3-x-directives memory: 'code review can't catch this; only live browser-automation verification can.'
close_reason:
Fixed in map.js: converted getClusterLeaves + getClusterExpansionZoom from the dropped maplibre-4 callback signature to the maplibre-5 Promise signature.

End-to-end verified via browser-automation hot-patch on switch.berlin/events/ before push:
1. Mixed cluster (17 events, 2 unique coords) clicked → zoom branch fires, easeTo from 10.56 → 12.
2. Co-located sub-cluster (16 IKSK at 13.426321,52.511692) clicked at zoom 12 → popup branch fires, header reads '16 events at this venue', 16 clickable links rendered.

Screenshots: /tmp/hot-patch-result.png, /tmp/hot-patch-result-2.png. Memory: maplibre-5x-cluster-callback-api-removed.

title: Root-cause DB password drift between prod deploys
description: Deploy 25666154527 (0724f2d, 11:01 UTC 2026-05-11) succeeded. The very next deploy 25671471540 (c9997cd) failed at the init container with 'password authentication failed for user postgres' against db@db:5432. .env DATABASE_URL was identical on both runs (gh secret unchanged). The DB volume was not recreated. Hypothesis: something mutated the postgres role password between the two deploys (no obvious culprit — no migration alters auth, seed_real_events doesn't either). I worked around it via 'ALTER USER postgres WITH PASSWORD postgres' on the live DB to realign with DATABASE_URL, but the root cause is unknown and likely to recur.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Identify the actor/process that altered the postgres role password between the two deploys (audit gh actions, /opt/switch-berlin logs, any cron, pg_stat_statements if available). (2) Either harden the deploy so password drift is impossible (e.g. always reset postgres password to .env DATABASE_URL value as part of init.sh, using peer auth) OR document the safe manual fix as a runbook. (3) Optional: remove 'host all all 127.0.0.1/32 trust' from pg_hba.conf so diagnose scripts can't false-positive.
notes: Root-caused 2026-05-12. Findings: (1) app-db-1 has NOT restarted since 2026-05-11 13:48 UTC — pg_authid is stable across the success→failure boundary. (2) Verified PGPASSWORD=postgres authenticates against the live DB. So pg_authid holds 'postgres'. (3) Every deploy since 2026-05-12 09:42 UTC fails because GH secret DATABASE_URL drifted to a value other than 'postgres' — .env is rewritten from secrets every deploy, so the app/init psycopg connection uses a password that no longer matches pg_authid. (4) Independent finding: docker-compose maps 5432:5432 unbound, exposing prod postgres to the public internet — db logs show active brute-force from 09:30 onward (database 'wog' probes, GRANT injection attempts). Filed as kb-bpc. Fix-forward: (a) docker-compose port → 127.0.0.1:5432:5432 (kb-bpc). (b) Self-healing deploy step in .github/workflows/deploy.yml: parse password from DATABASE_URL and ALTER USER postgres WITH PASSWORD via docker exec db psql -h 127.0.0.1 (trust-on-localhost bypasses auth, intentional for this purpose). ADRs: none directly. Related memories: prod-vps-compose-overlay-required.
close_reason: AC1 root-cause identified (GH secret DATABASE_URL drifted from pg_authid; .env rewritten every deploy — documented in notes). AC2 hardened: self-heal ALTER USER step in deploy.yml (commit 2af6a13, lines 108-130) idempotently realigns pg_authid to .env on every deploy. Verified by deploy 21d8f85 on 2026-05-13 — pipeline ran clean, all containers healthy, no auth failures in app/db logs. AC3 (optional: remove trust on 127.0.0.1) explicitly NOT done — the self-heal step now depends on that trust line to recover from password drift without already-broken creds.

title: Prod: Tailwind utilities missing from built CSS (templates not in vite build context)
description:
Prod app-<hash>.css is 13KB but contains only Tailwind preflight + theme — no utility classes (.btn, .card, .min-h-screen, etc.) and no DaisyUI components. Pages render unstyled.

Root cause: frontend/src/app.css uses Tailwind v4 @source directives pointing at ../../templates/**/*.html and ../../**/templates/**/*.html. The Dockerfile's frontend build stage only copies frontend/ into /build, so those @source globs resolve to /build/templates/ — which doesn't exist in that stage. Tailwind scans nothing, emits nothing.

Local dev works because tailwindcss/vite scans the full repo via vite dev server.
acceptance_criteria: Production app-<hash>.css contains DaisyUI/Tailwind utility classes (e.g. grep -c 'min-h-screen' /tmp/prod-app.css > 0). https://switch.berlin/age-check/ renders with card/btn styling instead of unstyled flow.
close_reason: Deployed in 85d155c: prod app-CXB4avt9.css is now 76KB (was 13KB) and contains .btn-primary, .card-body, .card-title, .min-h-screen. Page renders styled.

title: Prod: age-check page unstyled + CSRF 403 on submit
description:
Two production-breaking bugs hit on https://switch.berlin/age-check/:

1. **No styling**: page emits <script type=module src=/static/assets/app-cgn4pjPN.css> (a) wrong tag for CSS (django-vite vite_asset renders entries as script regardless of extension), (b) wrong URL — file actually lives at /static/dist/assets/... so whitenoise misses it and LoginWallMiddleware 302s to /accounts/login/. Net effect: no CSS loads on any unauthenticated page.

2. **CSRF 403** on POST /age-check/: SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER is unset, so behind Caddy's TLS termination Django sees request.scheme == http while the Origin header is https://switch.berlin. CsrfViewMiddleware's Origin/Referer check rejects the cross-scheme mismatch.

Repro: open https://switch.berlin/age-check/ in incognito → no styles. Click 'Yes, I am 18+' → 403 CSRF page.
acceptance_criteria: https://switch.berlin/age-check/ loads with full Tailwind/DaisyUI styling (card, btn classes render). Submitting the form with 'Yes, I am 18+' sets age_gate=ok cookie and redirects to / without a 403.
notes: Related: kb-2e3 covers broader prod security hardening (HSTS, SSL redirect, secure cookies). This bead applies only SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER as the minimum needed to unblock CSRF; kb-2e3 stays open for the rest.
close_reason: Deployed in 519ec18: CSS now renders as <link rel=stylesheet> at /static/dist/assets/app-cgn4pjPN.css (200 served by WhiteNoise); POST /age-check/ with valid CSRF returns 302 to / (verified via curl with X-Forwarded-Proto trusted).

title: Build Vite frontend assets during Docker image build
description: The production app container returns HTTP 500 because templates use {% vite_asset %} / {% vite_hmr_client %} (django_vite tags) but static/dist/.vite/manifest.json doesn't exist. The Dockerfile only installs Python deps and runs collectstatic — it never runs the frontend build. Locally devs use Vite's dev server (DJANGO_VITE_DEV_MODE) so the missing manifest is invisible.
design:
## Fix sketch
Multi-stage Dockerfile: add a node:22-slim builder stage that runs npm ci + npm run build in /frontend, then COPY --from=frontend /static/dist into /app/static/dist before collectstatic (so collectstatic picks up the built assets).

## Why P1
Blocks kb-6nq.6 acceptance (A.1 legal pages 200 + h1) — the deploy workflow itself is green but the app cannot serve any HTML view that extends _base.html (which loads vite_asset 'src/app.css').

title: Verify production deploy acceptance end-to-end
design:
## Scope

After all other slots are deployed/configured, the full epic acceptance contract (clauses A.1–A.4, B.1–B.5, C.1–C.3) is run as an explicit verification pass against the live production environment.

Each clause's mechanical probe is executed; results are recorded with pass/fail per clause. A clean pass on every clause unblocks closure of the epic. Failures route to the relevant implementation slot for remediation.

This slot is the integration verification gate — it asserts the cross-slot emergent behavior that no individual implementation slot covers in isolation.

Coverage targets: ALL A/B/C clauses (verification, not implementation).
acceptance_criteria:
All thirteen clauses of the epic's A/B/C acceptance contract are executed against the live production environment in a single verification pass, and each clause is recorded as pass or fail before this slot is closed.

**External probes:** All four public URLs return HTTP 200 with the expected heading (A.1); at least one referenced static asset per page returns 200 with a matching Content-Type (A.2); the TLS certificate issuer Organisation reads "Let's Encrypt" (A.3); a request to the www subdomain is redirected to the apex domain with a 301 or 308 status (A.4).

**On-host probes:** The migration check exits 0 (B.1); the deployment configuration check exits 0 (B.2); all four expected service containers are reported running and healthy (B.3); the backup timer's last-triggered timestamp is non-empty (B.4); a restic restore into an isolated scratch container produces a row count or schema checksum matching the source database (B.5).

**Gate posture:** The impressum contact address is confirmed as the designated protonmail address (C.1); the public-read flag is enabled and its origin is traced to the seeding migration, not a manual set (C.2); the deployment check exits 0 confirming the env-var population gate is satisfied (C.3).

**Verification record:** A pass/fail result is recorded per clause code (A.1 through C.3). Any failing clause routes to the relevant implementation slot for remediation; the epic is unblocked only when all thirteen clauses record pass.

title: Implement GH Actions deploy workflow
design:
## Scope

A GitHub Actions workflow exists in the repository at `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` that triggers on push to `main` and executes the D4 ordered steps end-to-end:

1. SSH into the VPS as the deploy user and pull `main` into the working directory.
2. Render `/opt/switch-berlin/.env` from GH Actions Secrets and non-secret workflow env (mode 600, owned by deploy user) — must complete before any compose invocation.
3. `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file /opt/switch-berlin/.env build app`.
4. `docker compose ... up -d --remove-orphans`.
5. `docker compose exec app python manage.py migrate --no-input` (apply pending migrations).
6. `docker compose exec app python manage.py migrate --check` (post-condition: exit 0 means no migrations pending).
7. `docker compose exec app python manage.py check --deploy` (blocking: fails workflow if non-zero).
8. `systemctl start kb-backup.service` to populate the timer's `LAST` column on first deploy.

A failed step short-circuits the workflow.

Coverage targets: A.1 (legal pages 200 + h1 — workflow brings app live), A.2 (static assets serve), B.1 (migrate --check exit 0), B.2 (check --deploy exit 0), B.3 (compose ps healthy), B.4 partial (workflow step 8 starts kb-backup.service), C.3 partial (workflow consumes slot-4 secrets and runs check --deploy).
acceptance_criteria:
A `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` file targeting the `main` branch is present in the repository.

A push to `main` produces a completed GH Actions workflow run with status "success" (no step exits non-zero, no step is skipped due to a prior failure).

At the conclusion of a green workflow run, all four compose services are observed as running or healthy on the VPS — verifiable via `docker compose ps` without manual intervention.

At the conclusion of a green workflow run, `manage.py migrate --check` exits 0 on the deployed container, confirming no pending migrations remain.

At the conclusion of a green workflow run, `manage.py check --deploy` exits 0 on the deployed container, confirming all required environment variables (including `IMPRESSUM_*`) are populated and the deployment system check is satisfied.
notes:
## ADRs consulted
- docs/decisions/ADR-001-core-product-and-stack.md
- docs/decisions/ADR-002-phased-rollout-and-legal-gate.md
- docs/decisions/ADR-006-legal-gate-execution.md

title: Provision backup subsystem on VPS (restic to Hetzner Storage Box)
design:
## Scope

A `kb-backup.service` systemd unit and `kb-backup.timer` exist on the VPS. The service performs `pg_dump` of the production Postgres container piped through `restic backup` to a Hetzner Storage Box repository. The timer is enabled at boot and scheduled nightly. The restic repository is initialized at the Storage Box destination (one-time bootstrap).

The service can be triggered manually via `systemctl start kb-backup.service`; the timer's `LAST` column populates after the first triggered run. Backup integrity is verifiable: the latest restic snapshot restores into a scratch container with `events_event` row count matching live ±1 if non-empty, or `pg_dump --schema-only` checksum matching live if empty.

Slot-3 owns the subsystem (units installed + timer enabled + restic repo initialized + manual run produces a verifiable snapshot). The first-deploy auto-trigger that populates the timer's `LAST` column is slot-5's workflow responsibility (avoids circular dep).

Coverage targets: B.4 (timer enabled + scheduled + LAST populated post-trigger), B.5 (restic snapshot restores).
acceptance_criteria:
The backup timer unit is reported as enabled by the system init manager, and when queried for scheduled state it shows a future NEXT trigger time.

A manual one-shot trigger of the backup service completes without error and leaves at least one snapshot visible in the restic repository at the Hetzner Storage Box destination.

The restic repository at the Storage Box destination is in an initialized state prior to any service run, confirmed by a snapshot-listing command returning successfully with zero snapshots and no initialization error.

A snapshot produced by a manual trigger is restorable into an isolated scratch context: if the live database contains rows in the events table, the restored row count matches the live count within one row; if the live database is empty, a schema-only export from the restored database produces a checksum identical to the same export from the live database.
notes:
## ADRs consulted
- docs/decisions/ADR-001-core-product-and-stack.md
- docs/decisions/ADR-002-phased-rollout-and-legal-gate.md
- docs/decisions/ADR-006-legal-gate-execution.md

title: Create docker-compose.prod.yml production overlay
design:
## Scope

A `docker-compose.prod.yml` overlay file exists in the repository. It adds `restart: unless-stopped` to all four services (`app`, `qcluster`, `bot`, `db`); declares host-bind-mount paths under `/opt/switch-berlin/` for the database volume; applies production resource limits where appropriate. It does NOT add or override services.

The base `docker-compose.yml` remains dev-safe; the prod overlay is composable with it. The production image, when built via this overlay, includes collected static assets per D7 (Whitenoise serves them; no runtime collectstatic needed).

This slot is a pure repo artifact — verifiable locally without a live VPS.

Coverage targets: A.2 partial (collected static assets present in image), B.3 partial (restart policies declared), supporting infrastructure for slot-5.
acceptance_criteria:
When the base and overlay files are merged via `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml config`, the command exits 0, producing a resolved config with no YAML errors, no unresolvable service references, and no volume or network collisions.

In that resolved config output, `restart: unless-stopped` is present on all four services (`app`, `qcluster`, `bot`, `db`).

In that resolved config output, the `db` service volume maps to a host bind-mount path rooted under `/opt/switch-berlin/` — no named `postgres_data` volume from the base file remains active in the merged result.

A production image built from the `app` service using the overlay contains a non-empty static-files directory — verified by inspecting the image filesystem without launching the container — confirming that static-asset collection occurred at build time rather than requiring a runtime step.

The base `docker-compose.yml` remains usable in isolation (without the overlay) and shows none of the prod-only additions: no `restart` policy on any service, no `/opt/switch-berlin/` bind-mount paths.

title: Provision Hetzner VPS, DNS, and Caddy TLS reverse proxy
design:
## Scope

A live Hetzner Cloud VPS in an EU region (Falkenstein or Nuremberg) is reachable on the public internet at `switch.berlin` and `www.switch.berlin`. Caddy is installed on the host and configured to terminate TLS via Let's Encrypt for both apex and `www`, with `www` redirecting to apex via 301/308. Caddy reverse-proxies application traffic to the compose stack (proxy upstream configured but app not yet running). The deploy user account and working directory `/opt/switch-berlin/` exist on the host. The `switch.berlin` domain's A/AAAA records at inwx point at the VPS public IP.

This slot delivers reachable infrastructure only — the application containers are not started here; that is slot-5's responsibility.

Coverage targets: A.3 (TLS issuer Let's Encrypt), A.4 (www→apex redirect), supporting infrastructure for B.3.
acceptance_criteria:
A DNS resolution of `switch.berlin` and `www.switch.berlin` each returns the VPS public IP address via an A record (IPv4) and/or AAAA record (IPv6).

When a TLS handshake is performed against `switch.berlin:443`, the certificate issuer Organisation field is `Let's Encrypt`.

An HTTPS request to any path under `https://www.switch.berlin/` receives a 301 or 308 redirect response pointing to the corresponding `https://switch.berlin/` URL; port 80 on either host responds with a redirect to HTTPS.

The VPS host contains an OS user account designated for deployments and the directory `/opt/switch-berlin/` exists and is owned by that account.
notes:
ACCEPTANCE PROBES (all green, run from laptop, post-DNS-propagation):

- dig +short switch.berlin A → 128.140.56.30 ✓
- dig +short switch.berlin AAAA → 2a01:4f8:c014:7cbc::1 ✓
- dig +short www.switch.berlin {A,AAAA} → same IPs ✓
- openssl s_client | openssl x509 -noout -issuer → 'O = Let'\''s Encrypt' (CN=E7) ✓
- curl -sI https://www.switch.berlin/ → 308 → https://switch.berlin/ ✓
- curl -sI http://switch.berlin/ → 308 (HTTP→HTTPS) ✓
- ssh switch@host 'stat -c %U /opt/switch-berlin' → switch ✓
- (apex returns 502 from / because no app upstream yet — kb-6nq.5; TLS still terminates correctly)

DEPLOYMENT GAP DISCOVERED + FIXED:
The 'caddy' debian package's postinst did NOT create the system user/group on Ubuntu 24.04 (status=217/USER). cloud-init.yaml updated with explicit groupadd/useradd block before package install loop. Future VPS rebuilds via this cloud-init will provision Caddy correctly without the manual fix-up.

DNS panel: Cloudflare (DNS-only / grey-cloud). Updated via API in /tmp/cf_dns_setup.py (token loaded from .env). 4 records: A/AAAA × @/www, all proxied=False.
close_reason: All 4 acceptance probes pass: DNS resolves to VPS, TLS issuer = Let's Encrypt, www→apex 308, /opt/switch-berlin owned by deploy user. Caddy user-creation gap fixed in cloud-init.yaml for re-provisioning.

  2. Necessity: no less-intrusive alternative; events are already public on source channels; we add discoverability, not new exposure.
  3. Balancing: organizers are semi-public figures acting in a public capacity; no special-category data about the organizer is processed; the opt-out path (/takedown/) is accessible without login and responds within 72h.
  4. Art. 21 opt-out path: reference the /takedown/ endpoint; describe the outcome (organizer listing hidden within 72h; event ingestion halted for that source).
  5. Review trigger: re-assess if 3+ organizer objections per quarter.

SCHEMA CHANGE (organizers/models.py):
  Current choices for consent_method:
    ("telegram_forward_implied", "Telegram forward (implied)")
  Add before existing:
    ("legitimate_interest", "Legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f))")

  Full new choices list:
    CONSENT_METHOD_CHOICES = [
        ("legitimate_interest", "Legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f))"),
        ("telegram_forward_implied", "Telegram forward (implied)"),
    ]

SCHEMA MIGRATION: standard Django migration to add the new choice (no DB column change, just choices kwarg update for documentation/admin dropdown).

DATA MIGRATION (separate migration file):
  from django.db import migrations

  def backfill_consent_method(apps, schema_editor):
      Organizer = apps.get_model("organizers", "Organizer")
      for org in Organizer.objects.filter(consent_method="telegram_forward_implied"):
          org.consent_method = "legitimate_interest"
          existing_notes = org.consent_notes or ""
          org.consent_notes = existing_notes + "\nMigrated to Art. 6(1)(f) per ADR-006 on 2026-04-22."
          org.save(update_fields=["consent_method", "consent_notes"])

  def reverse_backfill(apps, schema_editor):
      Organizer = apps.get_model("organizers", "Organizer")
      for org in Organizer.objects.filter(consent_method="legitimate_interest"):
          org.consent_method = "telegram_forward_implied"
          org.save(update_fields=["consent_method"])

  class Migration(migrations.Migration):
      dependencies = [("organizers", "0NNN_add_legitimate_interest_choice")]
      operations = [migrations.RunPython(backfill_consent_method, reverse_backfill)]

TESTS (tests/test_organizer_lia_migration.py):
  - After running migration forward: all previously telegram_forward_implied rows now have consent_method="legitimate_interest" and consent_notes contains "ADR-006"
  - Running migration twice (idempotency): rows not double-migrated; consent_notes not duplicated
  - Admin organizer change form shows "Legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f))" in dropdown
  - docs/compliance/organizer-lia.md exists and contains the words "Art. 6(1)(f)", "balancing", "takedown"
design: docs/plans/2026-04-22-legal-gate-bundle-design.md
acceptance_criteria: docs/compliance/organizer-lia.md exists with purpose/necessity/balancing/Art.21 sections. All telegram_forward_implied organizers backfilled to legitimate_interest with ADR-006 note in consent_notes. Migration is reversible and idempotent. Admin dropdown shows new choice. Tests pass.
notes: ADR-006 D2 is FIRM. Do not skip or defer the LIA document. The data migration must be reversible. Idempotency: running the migration twice must not append the note twice — check for existing note text before appending. No dependency on kb-804 or NEW-A; can land independently.

description:

SCHEMA (a_core/settings.py additions):

  IMPRESSUM_ADDRESS = os.environ.get('IMPRESSUM_ADDRESS', '')
  IMPRESSUM_EMAIL   = os.environ.get('IMPRESSUM_EMAIL', '')

  RESPONSIBLE_PERSON_NAME    = os.environ.get('RESPONSIBLE_PERSON_NAME', '') or IMPRESSUM_NAME
  RESPONSIBLE_PERSON_ADDRESS = os.environ.get('RESPONSIBLE_PERSON_ADDRESS', '') or IMPRESSUM_ADDRESS
  DSA_CONTACT_EMAIL = os.environ.get('DSA_CONTACT_EMAIL', '') or IMPRESSUM_EMAIL
  LEGAL_CONTACT = { 'name': IMPRESSUM_NAME, 'address': IMPRESSUM_ADDRESS, 'email': IMPRESSUM_EMAIL, 'phone': IMPRESSUM_PHONE, 'responsible_name': RESPONSIBLE_PERSON_NAME, 'responsible_address': RESPONSIBLE_PERSON_ADDRESS, 'dsa_email': DSA_CONTACT_EMAIL }

a_core/legal.py:
  from django.conf import settings
  def get_legal_contact():
      return settings.LEGAL_CONTACT

a_core/checks.py:
  from django.core.checks import Error, Warning, register
  REQUIRED_LEGAL_VARS = ['IMPRESSUM_NAME', 'IMPRESSUM_ADDRESS', 'IMPRESSUM_EMAIL']

  @register()
  def check_legal_contact(app_configs, **kwargs):
      from django.conf import settings
      from a_core.models import get_flag
      errors = []
      public_read = get_flag('PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED', default=False)
      missing = [v for v in REQUIRED_LEGAL_VARS if not getattr(settings, v, '')]
      if not missing:
          return errors
      if public_read:
          errors.append(Error(
              'PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED=True but required legal env vars are empty: ' + ', '.join(missing),
              hint='Set IMPRESSUM_NAME, IMPRESSUM_ADDRESS, IMPRESSUM_EMAIL in your environment.',
              obj=settings,
              id='a_core.E006',
          ))
      elif settings.DEBUG:
          errors.append(Warning(
              'Legal env vars are empty (OK for DEBUG): ' + ', '.join(missing),
              hint='Fill before setting PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED=True.',
              obj=settings,
              id='a_core.W006',
          ))
      return errors

  class ACoreConfig(AppConfig):

      def ready(self):
